messages.author: ba3c9b860132e9b2
messages.subject: getting timezones aligned in micro_era5()
parts:
Hi Mike, 

I'm currently trying to get downscaled air and ground temperatures using micro_era5(). I'm eventually trying to output air and ground temps for my field sites, but right now I'm simply following the example on your github here. Everything is fine until I run:

micro <- micro_era5(loc = loc, dstart = dstart, dfinish = dfinish, spatial = "/Users/laurenneel/Desktop/Spatial_Data/era5")

Then, I get an error message saying some data are in UTC/GMT timezone, and some are in PDT. I've attached a picture showing the full error message. I've tried figuring out how to get everything on the same timezone by looking at your source code, but I haven't had success yet. 

Is there by chance an easy fix for this?

Thanks in advance for the help!
Cheers,
Lauren

messages.author: 6cec8ea3702ece93
messages.subject: Re: getting timezones aligned in micro_era5()
parts:
Hi Lauren,

That shouldn't be a problem - it's a warning rather than an error. The time in ERA5 is UTC. The warning is not coming from a NicheMapR function but a microclima on, microclimaforNMR, and the relevant code is pasted below. You should just check that when you convert from the UTC of the output to a local time zone, it all  makes sense in terms of the timing of local solar noon etc.

All the best,
Mike

    tme <- seq(as.POSIXlt(dstart, format = "%d/%m/%Y",
        origin = "01/01/1900", tz = "UTC"), as.POSIXlt(dfinish,
        format = "%d/%m/%Y", origin = "01/01/1900",
        tz = "UTC") + 3600 * 24, by = "hours")
    tme2 <- seq(as.POSIXlt(dstart, format = "%d/%m/%Y",
        origin = "01/01/1900"), as.POSIXlt(dfinish, format = "%d/%m/%Y",
        origin = "01/01/1900") + 3600 * 24, by = "hours")
    tz1 <- format(as.POSIXlt(tme), format = "%Z")
    tz2 <- format(as.POSIXlt(tme2), format = "%Z")
    xx <- as.numeric(tme) == as.numeric(tme2)
    sel <- which(xx == FALSE)
    if (length(sel) > 1) {
        warning(paste("Data sequence in UTC/GMT. Some or all dates using system timezone are in",
            tz2[sel[1]]))
    }

parts:
Hi Mike, 

Thanks for the fast help! 

I think this makes sense. I'm pretty sure I was looking at data in UTC time and mistakenly thinking it was in local time, because the data I generated show max daily temps around 6-7am. So to clarify, do I convert from UTC to local time zone using the following lines of code?

tzone <- paste("Etc/GMT+", 0, sep="")
dates <- seq(as.POSIXct(dstart, format="%d/%m/%Y",tz=tzone)-3600*12, as.POSIXct(dfinish, format="%d/%m/%Y",tz=tzone)+3600*11, by="hours")

Except, since I'm in Arizona, to convert from UTC to local time I'd need to add 7 hours, so would I write:
tzone <- paste("Etc/GMT+", -7, sep="")

Lastly, I'm a bit confused about the code you've included above because I don't have any of those variables (tme, tme2, tz1, tz2) in my code. Could you briefly clarify what that code would be used for? It doesn't look familiar from any of the online examples or source code that I've read.

Thanks again! This is really helpful! 
Lauren

All the best,
Mike
